costGuide.title: Land Rover 204DTD Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 204DTD typically takes 10-14 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for a 204DTD engine replacement is the condition of the timing chain assembly and the EGR system. Units where the early-style tensioners have been upgraded to the revised post-2019 specification, and the EGR cooler has been replaced, command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Because this is a complex, modern common-rail engine, a full 204DTD rebuild requires specialist diagnostic equipment and precision machining. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for a detailed breakdown of what influences your final quote.

failures.title: Land Rover 204DTD Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure (Pre-2019 models)
items.whatHappens: Early Ingenium 2.0D units suffer from timing chain tensioner wear, leading to chain stretch, a distinct cold-start rattle, and potential catastrophic engine failure if the chain skips.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, the tensioner and chain can be replaced. However, if the chain has skipped and caused valve-to-piston contact, a full 204DTD engine replacement is required. Post-2019 revisions feature an updated tensioner design that largely resolves this issue.

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks and DPF Oil Dilution
items.whatHappens: The EGR cooler can develop internal cracks, leaking coolant into the exhaust or intake. Additionally, frequent short urban trips prevent active DPF regeneration, leading to fuel diluting the engine oil, which accelerates bearing wear.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the EGR cooler and adopting strict 6,000-mile oil change intervals are critical preventative measures. If oil dilution has caused bottom-end bearing damage, a full unit replacement is necessary.

items.title: Water Pump and Coolant Leaks
items.whatHappens: The plastic water pump housing and associated coolant pipes are prone to cracking and leaking, leading to coolant loss and potential overheating.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the water pump and upgrading to revised coolant pipes is a standard repair. If ignored, overheating can warp the cylinder head, necessitating a full engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2019 production units received a revised timing chain tensioner and improved EGR routing, making them significantly more robust than the earliest 2015-2018 examples .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 204DTD
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the dipstick tube or on the transmission bell housing mating surface, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The 204DTD is frequently confused with the older Ford-sourced Land Rover 224DT (which lacks the Ingenium architecture and has different ECU mapping) or the petrol sibling Land Rover 204PT. Fitting a 224DT or 204PT into a 204DTD vehicle requires extensive ECU remapping, different engine mounts, and altered fuel and exhaust architecture, making exact code matching critical to avoid costly installation errors.

relatives.description: - the Ford-sourced 2.2L Duratorq the 204DTD replaced in the Evoque and Freelander 2, which lacked the Ingenium architecture but offered cheaper, simpler repairs.
- the 3.0-litre inline-six Ingenium diesel introduced in 2020 for the Defender and Range Rover, offering more torque but a completely different cylinder layout and firing order.
- the 2.0-litre petrol Ingenium variant sharing the same block architecture, which is generally considered more reliable than the diesel but requires different ECU mapping and fuel system components.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 204DTD - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 204DTD is only advisable if it is a post-2019 revision with verifiable proof of strict 6,000-mile oil changes and no history of EGR or DPF issues. Pre-2019 units carry an unacceptably high risk of inheriting timing chain tensioner wear. Explore our vetted used 204DTD engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 204DTD addresses the core weaknesses of the early Ingenium D. It will include an upgraded timing chain tensioner, a refreshed EGR cooler, and a thoroughly flushed oil system to remove any DPF oil dilution residue. This is the most sensible route for preserving a Discovery Sport or Evoque. Compare reconditioned 204DTD options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing early signs of bearing wear from oil dilution, or if the engine has already suffered timing chain skip damage. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new bearings, and a complete overhaul of the valvetrain to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom 204DTD rebuild

items.question: What is the most common failure on the 204DTD?
items.answer: The dominant failure patterns on the 204DTD are timing chain tensioner failure on pre-2019 models, EGR cooler leaks, and oil dilution from DPF regeneration. Early hydraulic tensioners can fail, causing chain stretch and a distinct cold-start rattle that can lead to catastrophic valve damage. EGR coolers can crack internally, leading to coolant loss and potential hydro-locking. Post-2019 revisions feature an updated tensioner design that largely resolves the timing chain issue.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the 204DTD engine?
items.answer: The 2.0L 204DTD Ingenium diesel was fitted to the Discovery Sport (L550), Range Rover Evoque (L538/L551), Range Rover Velar (L560), and Defender (L663) from 2015 onwards. It replaced the older Ford and PSA-sourced 2.2-litre units across Land Rover's compact and mid-size SUV range. It is mechanically distinct from the later 3.0-litre AJ20D6 and the petrol 204PT. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 204DTD engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned 204DTD is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known age-related weaknesses of the early timing chain tensioners and EGR system. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting a failing tensioner or a cracked EGR cooler. Proper reconditioning proactively upgrades these specific weak points with revised tensioners and refreshed EGR components. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the 204DTD and not the older 224DT or newer 204PT?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the dipstick tube. The 204DTD is visually identifiable by its specific Ingenium common-rail injection pump and turbo plumbing, lacking the older Ford Duratorq architecture. It is commonly confused with the petrol 204PT, which shares the same block but has entirely different fuel system and ECU mapping. Fitting the wrong revision will cause severe compatibility and mapping issues.
